identity.name: Bangkok Post
identity.description: Thailand's oldest English-language daily, covering Thai politics, business, society and Southeast Asian affairs.

ownership.ownershipNotes: Listed publisher Post Publishing PCL. Major shareholders include Suthikiati Chirathivat and Bangkok Bank, giving the paper close ties to Thai business elites.

editorialOrientation.evidence: Commercial newspaper with a professional English-language newsroom, but Thai media face legal and commercial pressure and the paper has elite ownership ties.
editorialOrientation.source: Ownership and self-description via secondary references (official about page blocked or unavailable); secondary references; feed-level sample

politicalLeaning.evidence: No parsed MBFC rating; self-assessed as broadly centrist with a pro-establishment and business-friendly orientation.
politicalLeaning.source: Analyst assessment from publisher self-description, secondary references and feed-level sample

economicPerspective.evidence: Business and tourism coverage generally favours market-friendly policy and foreign investment.
economicPerspective.source: Analyst assessment from business and economic coverage

internationalAlignment.evidence: Thai national and ASEAN lens with a strong business and tourism focus.
internationalAlignment.source: Ownership, editorial positioning and regional coverage sample

reliability.evidence: Established newspaper of record with named reporters and corrections; no external rating parsed.
reliability.source: Analyst assessment from ownership, editorial record and feed-level sample

externalRatings.notes: No MBFC rating identified for Bangkok Post.

intelligence.knownPerspective: Thai newspaper-of-record coverage in English. It explains Thai politics and business for expatriate and regional audiences.

selectionRationale: Adds Thai national coverage and a Southeast Asian business perspective.

research.researchNotes: Official About page returned 404. Ownership from 2026 AGM reporting and Wikipedia; requires human verification because shareholder detail is time-sensitive. Research is feed-level only; full article sampling and peer review remain outstanding.
